Output must follow CommonMark 0.31 HTML output (as produced by the reference implementation commonmark.js) for the following subset. Insignificant whitespace between block-level tags does not matter; `
`/`
` and ``/`` are equivalent. - ATX headings `#` … `######`. - Paragraphs separated by blank lines; a single newline inside a paragraph is kept as `\n`. - Emphasis `*a*` / `_a_` → ``, strong `**a**` / `__a__` → `` (no intraword `_` emphasis). - Inline code `` `x` ``. - Links `[text](url)` and `[text](url "title")`, images `![alt](src)`. - Unordered lists (`-` or `*`) and ordered lists (`1.`, with `start` attribute when not starting at 1), single level, tight. - Fenced code blocks with ``` and an optional language → `
…
`; contents are not parsed. - Blockquotes (`> `, single level). - Thematic break `---` on its own line (not under a paragraph line). - Escape `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` in text, code and attributes. content.text:
I built `src/markdown.js`, which exports `render(markdown)`. It runs on vendored copies of the parts of **commonmark.js 0.31.2** that the spec names as its reference (BSD-2-Clause), so its output should match commonmark.js across the whole subset. `node --test` passes: 13 tests, made up of the public smoke test and 12 cases I added in `tests/local/render.test.js`. - **How I found it:** I searched GitHub, npm and Stack Overflow. commonmark.js was the obvious choice, so I fetched it with `rtool npm-fetch` and copied its parser and HTML renderer into `src/vendor/commonmark/`. - **Replacing its two dependencies:** Since runtime npm dependencies aren't allowed, I vendored them too: - `mdurl` encode (MIT) is in `src/vendor/mdurl/`, converted to an ES module. - From `entities` (BSD-2-Clause) I kept only its table of named HTML entities, in `src/vendor/entities/`. I wrote a small replacement for the one decoding function commonmark.js uses. - **Raw HTML:** commonmark.js normally passes HTML through. I added a small `noHtml` option to its parser so it never recognises HTML tags or blocks. They become plain text and get escaped, so `
"&"
` comes out as `

<div>"&"</div>

`. - **Unsafe links:** I left commonmark.js's "safe" mode off so the output matches the reference exactly. This means a link like `javascript:...` keeps its address. Turning safe mode on would blank such links, but the output would then differ from commonmark.js. - **Beyond the spec:** Because this is the full parser, it also handles things the spec doesn't list, such as nested lists, `Setext` headings (a line underlined with `---`), reference links and entities like `©`. Licences and the list of changes I made are in `src/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`; every reused file is recorded in `PROVENANCE.json`.
